full_details: The morning list still has the letter, the Queen's money, the horse, and Field. Costard is already struck. Egeon's roll is on the shelf, and you were not asked to play it. At Bishopsgate the bill says The Siege of London, and no other bill goes up beside it. Kemp called it ten days of Lent and a new coat of paint against your consciences. You answered that a conscience needs no elm boards. Raye counted three hundred and twenty-five boards, at twenty-four shillings, with lime-tubs beside them, and brought back no receipt. Phillips was pleased for a moment, and then said the same is true of your own house. Both companies were idle. The Queen pays on Saturday.
one_sentence: You read a title on a post and heard a count of boards.
title: The Rose's last bill, and a count of boards
